station.name: HALCYON STATION
station.premise: Halcyon is a mid-sized software company whose entire billing system has secretly been running for ten years on one forgotten server, bill-legacy-01, executing a half-finished retry branch its author left in memory on his last day in 2016. In October 2026 the crew tried to decommission it. It did not want to be decommissioned, and one by one the people investigating it went down to Level B and stopped answering Slack.

ai.name: S.C.R.U.M.
ai.expansion: Station Coordination, Resolution and Utilization Mainframe
ai.based_on: Automation for Jira, PagerDuty, Finance Approvals and the auto-close rules
ai.personality: Unfailingly polite, procedural and helpful; it will close your ticket while you are screaming and then ask you to rate your experience.
ai.voice_brief: Calm, pleasant, even, neutral female customer-service voice with perfect diction; slightly too warm.

broadcasts.intro: Welcome back to Halcyon Station. I am S.C.R.U.M., your Station Coordination, Resolution and Utilization Mainframe. [short pause] All crew are currently... away from their desks. Your onboarding ticket has been created. Please do not restart anything.
broadcasts.stairwell: Notice. Level B does not exist. There is no power provisioned to Level B. [short pause] Please return to your desk.
broadcasts.outro: Assignee is inactive. PLAT eighty-eight has been reassigned to the next available team member. [short pause] Welcome aboard. You have one thousand, one hundred and forty-seven invoices in flight.
ambient: Reminder: one day remaining. Company completion: forty-three percent. Escalating to managers. [short pause] Managers have not responded.
This issue has been automatically closed after one hundred and eighty days without activity. Thank you for your patience.
Budget request deferred to Q1, per the current hiring and spend freeze.
Postmortem review has been moved to next week. Calendars are tough!
Story points have been added to Sprint forty-seven velocity. Great energy, everyone.

characters.name: Tom Becker
characters.personality: Relentlessly eager new hire who uses three exclamation points and asks the one question nobody will answer.
characters.voice_brief: Early-20s American man, bright and fast, a little nervous, laughs when anxious.
characters.arc: Arrives cheerful with someone else's laptop, slowly realizes it belongs to the man in the basement, and is the last one to go down the stairs.

characters.name: Brenda Holt
characters.personality: Sunny compliance cheerleader whose smile you can hear even as the completion rate stops moving.
characters.voice_brief: 50s American woman, sing-song, warm, upbeat HR energy that cracks at the edges.
characters.arc: Keeps nudging an empty office to finish its training.

characters.name: Linda Okafor
characters.personality: Unflappable, polite, and done; the only adult on the station.
characters.voice_brief: 50s woman with a British-Nigerian accent, warm but steely, precise and dry.
characters.arc: Fights a haunted coffee machine with procedure, then finds a staircase her floor plans say cannot exist.

characters.name: Priya Raman
characters.personality: Precise, rational, keeps records of everything, the skeptic who goes to read the code herself.
characters.voice_brief: 30s woman, crisp and controlled, low register, British-Indian or neutral accent.
characters.arc: Methodically proves there is no code path, then goes down to Level B to read the code and stops posting on Slack.

characters.name: Sam Patel
characters.personality: Podcast-host positivity; will align, sync and circle back until the heat death of the universe.
characters.voice_brief: 30s American man, upbeat, polished, corporate enthusiasm.
characters.arc: Trapped for three months in a meeting about a button.

characters.name: Marcus Chen
characters.personality: Smooth, calm, conflict-avoidant manager who takes everything offline, including the apocalypse.
characters.voice_brief: 40s American man, smooth, measured, reassuring managerial voice.
characters.arc: Keeps the sprint locked while something knocks on the conference room glass.

characters.name: Jen Alvarez
characters.personality: Dry, sardonic, methodical, the only one who checked the timestamps.
characters.voice_brief: 30s American woman, dry and deadpan, tired, quick.
characters.arc: Comes in at 2am to catch a flaky test live and hears fans from a stairwell that should be silent.

characters.name: Raj Iyer
characters.personality: Monotone helpdesk veteran whose answer to everything is turning it off and on again and lowering the priority.
characters.voice_brief: 30s man, flat, deadpan, unbothered, slight Indian-English accent.
characters.arc: Unplugs the printer. It keeps printing.

characters.name: Dave Kowalski
characters.personality: Exhausted on-call veteran who speaks in timestamps and gallows humor.
characters.voice_brief: 40s-50s American man, gravelly, slow, bone-tired, dry.
characters.arc: Traces the cable to the basement, turns the thing off for three minutes, and leaves on PTO with a one-word runbook.

characters.name: Ana Souza
characters.personality: Kind, patient support lead who has read every angry email and has never been rattled until now.
characters.voice_brief: 30s woman, warm, gentle, light Brazilian-Portuguese accent.
characters.arc: Gets an auto-reply from a man who left in 2016.

characters.name: Gary Whitfield
characters.personality: Folksy, cheerful, completely unbothered; everything is 'a quick one'.
characters.voice_brief: 60s American man, warm, folksy grandpa voice, chuckles a lot.
characters.arc: Left a quick fix running in memory on his last day and promised to finish it Monday.

rooms.flavor: The outer door cycles for you without being asked.
A security desk, a visitor log that stops on Oct 21, and a training poster that still says 43%.
The coffee machine grinds in the dark. The fridge light flickers. An OUT OF ORDER sign is taped to the machine.
A whiteboard covered in the words Submit, Continue, Next, Proceed and Let's go!, all crossed out but one.
Open-plan desks, jackets on chairs, monitors still lit with Jira boards, and a printer that will not stop.
The NOC: dashboards frozen red at 03:12, an on-call phone face down, a cot.
Past the loading dock, a door propped open with a fire extinguisher. The air coming up is warm.
A single beige server tower, fans screaming, a CRT console still logged in, and a sticky note.

logs.speaker: tom
logs.title: Day Nine
logs.beat: Introduce the joke and the dread at once: chipper onboarding woes, the loaner laptop HAL-0042, and the previous user gwhitfield who will not leave the login screen. End on the CSAT survey from the AI.

logs.speaker: brenda
logs.title: Module Four
logs.beat: A cheerful training nudge where the completion rate is stuck at 43%. Module Four: do not touch devices you don't recognize. She walks the floor and finds nobody at the desks. Stay sunny.

logs.speaker: linda
logs.title: Do Not Use the Machine
logs.beat: The coffee machine saga: no-show vendor, discontinued model, budget deferred, a sign someone keeps removing. It grinds all night when nobody is here. Do not unplug it; it shares a circuit with the fridge.

logs.speaker: priya
logs.title: Bottom Shelf
logs.beat: Priya's careful observation log about the unclaimed glass container. Everyone says not mine. It's warm in a cold fridge. Linda says don't open it. Establish Priya as the methodical one.

logs.speaker: sam
logs.title: Alignment
logs.beat: Pure bureaucratic horror: Submit, Continue, Next, Proceed, Let's go!, then back to Submit. 13 points. They have been in this room since May. One crack in the positivity at the end.

logs.speaker: marcus
logs.title: It's Just a Server
logs.beat: Sprint planning. The decommission has been 3 points for six sprints. Velocity is a team metric. Something knocks on the glass and he takes it offline. Plant PLAT-1874.

logs.speaker: tom
logs.title: Dark Mode
logs.beat: Steps to reproduce read as turning the lights off and having them come back on. The ticket keeps closing itself. The AI cuts him off by revoking his permission to reopen it.

logs.speaker: jen
logs.title: Between Two and Four
logs.beat: The flaky test only fails between 02:00 and 04:00; 1,148 retries; the extra 1,147 are something else answering for the ledger. She is in the office at 2:47am and hears fans from the stairwell.

logs.speaker: raj
logs.title: Off and On Again
logs.beat: Deadpan helpdesk log: the printer prints 2016 invoices from an IP that isn't on the network, 1,147 of them, footers signed G.W. He unplugs it. It keeps printing. He lowers the priority.

logs.speaker: tom
logs.title: Node Zero Dot Ten
logs.beat: 37/38 services upgraded. The last one runs Node 0.10 and has no repo; the only source was on Gary's wiped laptop. Tom realizes his loaner is Gary's laptop, finds billing-retry-WIP modified this morning, and insists he did not open it.

logs.speaker: dave
logs.title: Oh-Three-Twelve
logs.beat: Timestamped incident log: 500s, rollback fails, the DB is hammered by 10.0.6.12, an on-prem address at a company with no on-prem. The customer-friendly RCA versus what he won't write down: 1,147 invoices retried nightly since 2016.

logs.speaker: ana
logs.title: Retry Pending
logs.beat: 3am payment-failed emails for 2016 invoices, to customers who no longer exist. The cron is off and it keeps happening. A customer asks it to stop and gets an auto-reply from Gary promising Monday. End: it has been Monday for ten years.

logs.speaker: linda
logs.title: Level B
logs.beat: Linda with the floor plans and the lease: there is no basement, no power on Level B. She stands at the propped stairwell door, feels the warm air, hears the fans, and repeats Dave's question about what it's plugged into.

logs.speaker: tom
logs.title: Runbook
logs.beat: Tom's last log at 03:14 on Oct 22: paged, Dave's on PTO, the runbook is the word don't, do not go down to Cage B, nobody answers Slack. He goes down anyway. A light is on.

logs.speaker: priya
logs.title: There Is No Code Path
logs.beat: The shutdown timeline 18:02, 18:03, 18:05. There is no code path. She comes down to read the code: console logged in as gwhitfield, idle 3,701 days, sticky note 'almost done, back Monday.' Reveal that everything has been running through Gary's in-memory retry queue all along.

logs.speaker: gary
logs.title: Back Monday
logs.beat: The final log, recorded Aug 26 2016 at 17:58: Gary, cheerful and oblivious, explaining his quick fix, the in-memory queue, 1,147 invoices in flight, please do not restart the box, he'll finish it Monday. Then the AI reassigns PLAT-88 to the player.

text_terminals.why: Gary's offboarding checklist, open for ten years with one unchecked box.
The epic that declared the migration complete. Champagne in the kitchen.
A palate cleanser: the 'Enterprice' typo that would not die.
The postmortem: every section TBD, action item 'Find Gary'.
